flagged_for_v413: Counterexample-guided re-induction from rejecting execution states (arXiv:2606.11521; SMT-checked CEGIS predecessor arXiv:2309.16436)

methods.name: Counterexample-Guided Learning in the Large
methods.pitfalls: The paper studies regex induction, not ARC games; Carnot must translate execution failures into compact, replayable grid/game counterexamples and avoid treating feedback as a live solve claim.
methods.what_it_takes_over_our_stack: Turn every verifier-rejected generic operator run into structured feedback: rejected state, expected predicate, observed predicate, and counterexample cluster. Re-prompt the inducer with that state until dc22, tr87, or sc25 reproduces under the offline env.

methods.name: LLM plus SMT counterexample-guided inductive synthesis
methods.pitfalls: Blocks-world planning is simpler than ARC-AGI-3; incomplete SMT encodings or hand-written constraints can launder game-specific knowledge into the induction loop.
methods.what_it_takes_over_our_stack: Use exact execution checks or small SMT encodings as the verifier that returns counterexamples to the LLM learner before any generic rule is accepted.

methods.name: SOAR self-improving evolutionary ARC synthesis
methods.pitfalls: Fine-tuning and self-improvement are outside this CPU-only ingestion; any future training must separate held-out games and avoid replay leakage.
methods.what_it_takes_over_our_stack: Wrap the re-induction loop in evolutionary search and bank verified repair attempts as hindsight examples for future generic operators.

methods.name: Neurally-guided ARC program induction
methods.pitfalls: A narrow DSL can miss mechanics, while an unconstrained DSL can explode search; the verifier must remain the authority.
methods.what_it_takes_over_our_stack: Constrain tr87-style glyph rewrite synthesis to a small grid DSL and use a learned prior only to order executable candidates.

methods.name: Induction plus transduction routing for ARC
methods.pitfalls: Static ARC input-output success does not prove interactive control; transductive shortcuts need separate action and state validation.
methods.what_it_takes_over_our_stack: Route each open gap between precise induced programs and direct state/output prediction, then require the chosen path to reproduce through the same offline gate.

methods.name: Executable ARC-AGI-3 world models
methods.pitfalls: Fresh workspaces and leakage audits are load-bearing; closed-agent headline numbers are not evidence that Carnot solved anything.
methods.what_it_takes_over_our_stack: Use the induce-verify-refactor-plan harness as the phase-FSM test bed for sc25 and other interactive games after a rule re-induces.

methods.name: Loop-OWM object-centric transition loops
methods.pitfalls: ARC-1/2 visual-symbolic transition prediction is not the same as interactive game planning; add goal, action-cost, and reproduction checks.
methods.what_it_takes_over_our_stack: Represent cast-grid, toggle, and glyph mechanics as slots plus looped object-state transitions before translating them into generic world-model operators.

methods.name: ARC living survey meta-solver context
methods.pitfalls: A survey is context, not a runnable method; it must not be counted as experimental evidence or a leaderboard result.
methods.what_it_takes_over_our_stack: Use the survey's cross-paradigm map to keep .413 focused on refinement loops, program synthesis, and interactive transfer instead of another single-model prompt sweep.

sota_to_experiment_mapping_note: SOTA->experiment map for .413: promote counterexample-guided re-induction from rejecting execution states (arXiv:2606.11521) as the strongest handoff, with SMT-checked CEGIS (arXiv:2309.16436) as the formal loop template. Feed verifier-rejected dc22, tr87, and sc25 execution states back into the generic operator prompt, cluster the failures, re-induce the rule, and accept only reproduction-gated fixes. Use SOAR (arXiv:2507.14172) and neurally-guided induction (arXiv:2411.17708) for search pressure, induction+transduction (arXiv:2411.02272) for routing, Executable World Models (arXiv:2605.05138) plus Loop-OWM (arXiv:2606.12316) for phase-FSM and object-state tests, and the ARC survey (arXiv:2603.13372) as the meta-solver context.
